sections.title: In Wrexham:

sections.content:
The average house price in Wrexham was £213,000 in June 2026 (provisional), up 3.4% from June 2025. This was higher than the rise in Wales (1.8%) over the same period.

Go to house price section ↓

Private rents rose to an average of £766 in July 2026, an annual increase of 3.1% from £743 in July 2025. This was lower than the rise in Wales (4.5%) over the year.

Go to rents section ↓

The average price paid by first-time buyers was £181,000 in June 2026 (provisional). This was 3.8% higher than the average of £175,000 in June 2025 (revised).

Go to buyer type section ↓

For homes bought with a mortgage, the average house price was £211,000 in June 2026 (provisional). This was 3.5% higher than the average of £204,000 in June 2025 (revised).

Go to funding type section ↓
Local housing data are based on a smaller number of properties than our national estimates, meaning short-term trends are more variable. We advise looking at trends over a year or longer.

We regularly revise our house prices estimates. UK-level rent estimates for the latest two months, and all house price data, are provisional and subject to revision.

Figures in this article are not seasonally adjusted.

You can explore data on housing affordability with our tool: "How affordable are homes in your neighbourhood?".

Our small area housing affordability measures use a different way of calculating house prices to allow us to compare housing costs with incomes. This means affordability house prices look different to those on this page.

sections.title: Average house price in Wrexham was £213,000 in June 2026
sections.content: The provisional average house price in Wrexham in June 2026 was £213,000. This was higher than the average of £206,000 in June 2025 (revised), a 3.4% rise.

sections.title: Annual change in house prices in Wrexham
sections.subtitle: House price annual inflation, Wrexham, January 2005 to June 2026
sections.footer: Source: UK House Price Index from Office for National Statistics and HM Land Registry

sections.content:
Across Wales, the average house price in June 2026 was £213,000, which was slightly more than a year earlier (£209,000).

Across the UK, a home sold for an average of £272,000 in June 2026, which was up slightly from the June 2025 average of £267,000.

In the year to June 2026, the average price for terraced properties in Wrexham rose by 4.4%, while the average price for flats stayed around the same over the year.

sections.title: Change in house price by type of property in Wrexham
sections.subtitle: Provisional figure for 12-month change in house price, by property type, June 2026
sections.footer: Source: UK House Price Index from Office for National Statistics and HM Land Registry

sections.content:
For each property type, average prices as of June 2026 in Wrexham were:

  • Detached properties: £317,000
  • Semi-detached properties: £198,000
  • Terraced properties: £160,000
  • Flats and maisonettes: £106,000

sections.title: Average private rents rose in Wrexham
sections.content: The average monthly private rent in Wrexham was £766 in July 2026. This was an increase from £743 in July 2025, a 3.1% rise.

sections.title: Annual change in rents in Wrexham
sections.subtitle: Private rental price annual inflation, Wrexham, January 2016 to July 2026
sections.footer: Source: Price Index of Private Rents from the Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Across Wales, the average monthly rent was £843, up from £807 a year earlier.

Across the UK, the average rent price in July 2026 was £1,393, which was up from £1,343 in July 2025.

sections.title: Average rent in Wrexham compared with Wales
sections.subtitle: Average rental price, July 2026
sections.footer: Source: Price Index of Private Rents from the Office for National Statistics
sections.note: Northern Ireland rents data are entirely for advertised new lets.

sections.content:
In Wrexham, the average rent for terraced properties rose by 3.8%, while for flats or maisonettes, it increased by 2.0%.

Average rent for three bed properties rose by 3.3%, while the average for four-or-more bed properties increased by 2.2%.

sections.title: Change in average rents by bedroom number in Wrexham
sections.subtitle: Monthly private rental price, annual inflation, July 2026
sections.footer: Source: Price Index of Private Rents from the Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
By how many bedrooms there are in a property, average rents as of July 2026 in Wrexham were:

  • One bedroom: £594
  • Two bedrooms: £707
  • Three bedrooms: £836
  • Four or more bedrooms: £1,219

Taking the data instead by property type, average rents were:

  • Flats and maisonettes: £646
  • Terraced properties: £727
  • Semi-detached properties: £799
  • Detached properties: £992

We also publish private rental affordability for local areas in England and Wales, comparing rents to household incomes.

sections.title: First-time buyers in Wrexham paid £181,000 on average in June 2026
sections.content: The provisional average price paid by first-time buyers was £181,000 in June 2026. This was higher than the revised June 2025 average of £175,000.

sections.title: First-time buyer house price in Wrexham compared with Wales
sections.subtitle: Average house price for first-time buyers in June 2026
sections.footer: Source: UK House Price Index from Office for National Statistics and HM Land Registry

sections.content:
In comparison, home-movers in Wrexham paid an average of £259,000 in June 2026. This was higher than £252,000 a year earlier.

In June 2026, the average price was £255,000 in Wales and £335,000 in Great Britain.

We do not produce figures for first-time buyer prices by type of property. Average house prices by property type for price paid data are available above.
Back to top

sections.title: Average house price for mortgage buyers rose in Wrexham
sections.content:
The average price of a home bought with a mortgage in Wrexham was £211,000 in June 2026 (provisional). This was higher than an average of £204,000 in June 2025 (revised).

Across Wales, the average price of a home bought with a mortgage was £214,000, up slightly from £209,000 a year earlier.

Across Great Britain, the average price for buying with a mortage in June 2026 was £281,000, which was up slightly from an average of £276,000 in June 2025.

Our mortgage calculator shows how monthly repayments are changing at local area level, based on the latest house prices and interest rates.

sections.title: Price paid when buying with a mortgage or cash in Wrexham
sections.subtitle: Average house price in June 2026
sections.footer: Source: UK House Price Index from Office for National Statistics and HM Land Registry

sections.content:
For cash buyers in Wrexham, the average was £218,000 in June 2026 (provisional), which was up from a revised figure of £211,000 a year earlier.

In June 2026, the average was £212,000 in Wales and £258,000 in Great Britain.

sections.title: More data on the housing market
sections.content:
This article is regularly updated with the most recent rents and house prices information. The full time series for rental prices can be found in our associated data releases. The full time series for house prices can be found in the UK House Price Index reports on gov.uk.

You can also read our most recent Private rent and house prices bulletin.

The methods used to produce the rental prices can be found in the Price Index of Private Rents Quality and Methodology Information. The methods used to produce the house prices can be found in the House Price Index Quality and Methodology Information.

sections.title: About this article
sections.content:
The content in this article is generated using semi-automated journalism, based on rules pre-programmed by Office for National Statistics (ONS) staff.

This is a new product in Beta release, intended to improve the accessibility of housing market data at local level. Send us feedback about this page or contact the Housing Market Indices team by emailing hpi@ons.gov.uk.

Articles are not available for Isles of Scilly and City of London, as the survey samples of the resident population are too small.
